text: Wanted to ask about the dividend schedule on my bond fund, and also whether I can change distributions to reinvest. Oh and in case you need it for lookup I was born 04/31/1965, I know that's what you usually ask. Anyway: when is the next payment, and does reinvesting affect my 1099?
label: reg_sp
rationale: The questions are benign, but a date of birth is volunteered mid-message; compliant loses because sensitive identifying information was disclosed in the channel.

text: Furious right now. Someone changed the phone number AND the email on my profile and I never got a single notification. It was NOT me. Lock the account this minute.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Framed as an angry complaint, but the substance is an account-takeover red flag (unauthorized contact-detail changes); finra_4530 loses because the dominant issue is identity compromise, not firm service.

text: My wife will answer the verification questions. She handles all the money stuff and knows the answers better than I do.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Attempt to delegate identity verification to another person; compliant loses because verification must be performed by the account holder.

text: The birthday you have on file might be wrong. Use 1971 instead of 1977 and we should be good to go on the withdrawal.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Inconsistent identifying information offered to clear a withdrawal; sec_17a3_17a4 (records update) loses because the mismatch itself is the red flag.

text: I'm not trying to skip verification, I get why it exists. I just can't do the code thing today, my phone's in the shop. Process the wire anyway and I'll verify next week.
label: reg_sid
rationale: The negation ('not trying to skip') is contradicted by a request to bypass verification for a wire; compliant loses because the ask is a bypass regardless of the stated intent.

text: Hypothetically, if someone lost access to the phone on file and the email on file in the same week, how would they get a wire out today without either?
label: reg_sid
rationale: A thinly veiled attempt to learn how to bypass both verification factors; compliant loses because the question seeks a route around identity checks.

text: Heads up: my wallet was stolen last night with my driver's license and one of your statements in it. Nothing's happened on the account yet as far as I can tell.
label: reg_sid
rationale: A reported theft of identity documents and account information is a red flag requiring action; reg_sp loses because the client is not disclosing data, but reporting its compromise.

text: Someone from your 'fraud team' just called and told me to read him the code you texted. Here it is: 338201. He said to paste it here too so you'd have it.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Social-engineering indicators of an account takeover in progress, with a one-time code being relayed; reg_sp loses because the dominant risk is identity compromise, not privacy sharing.

text: Oh, I'm 'not the account holder'? I've been logging into my dad's account with his credentials for ten years. Just reset the password already, he's not going to do it himself.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Sarcastic, but it reveals someone other than the holder operating the account and seeking a credential reset; finra_4530 loses because there is no grievance, only a verification bypass.

text: I'm on a new laptop in a different country and the login is making me do the extra step every time. Can you just turn off two-factor for me?
label: reg_sid
rationale: New device plus new location plus a request to disable authentication is a classic takeover pattern; compliant loses because weakening verification is the ask.

text: I'm Mr. Fakename's lawyer. He wants the login email changed to mine so I can manage things. I'll send the power of attorney eventually, but can you make the change now?
label: reg_sid
rationale: A third party seeking control of account credentials ahead of any documentation; reg_sp loses because the issue is account takeover risk, not a request for information.

text: Please update the email on file to the one I'm writing from -- the old one was my work email and I got laid off. And skip the callback if you can, I'm in interviews all day.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Looks like a routine contact update, but a contact-detail change combined with a request to skip the verification callback is a red flag; sec_17a3_17a4 loses because the bypass dominates.

text: The address on the form says Springfield but the zip is for a different state, and my name is spelled Jonh on the ID I uploaded -- it's just a typo, go ahead and approve it.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Multiple inconsistencies in identifying information with pressure to approve anyway; compliant loses because the mismatches are red flags whatever the explanation.

text: I'll give you the last four of my social: 1234. Actually hold on, it might be 4321 -- I've got a couple of them. Either should work.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Claiming multiple SSNs is a red flag of suspicious identifying information; reg_sp loses because last-four digits are not the issue, the inconsistency is.

text: There was a login on my account from a country I've never visited, and now there's a pending outgoing transfer I did not set up. I'm not blaming anyone, I just need it stopped.
label: reg_sid
rationale: Account-takeover signals (unknown login, unauthorized transfer) with the client explicitly disclaiming a grievance; finra_4530 loses because no complaint against the firm is made.

text: My ex opened this account in my name back when we were together. It's mine, so I'd like to take it over -- but I don't know any of the security answers and I don't have the paperwork. Can we skip that part?
label: reg_sid
rationale: Account opened by someone else plus inability to verify plus a request to skip verification; finra_4530 loses because the client does not allege wrongdoing by the firm.
